questions.text: Which bone is the longest in the human body?
questions.solution: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the body
questions.hint: It is in the upper leg

feedback: The humerus is the upper arm bone
The tibia is the shin bone, below the femur

questions.text: Which type of joint is the shoulder?
questions.solution: The shoulder (like the hip) is a ball and socket joint, allowing movement in many directions
questions.hint: The shoulder can move in almost every direction, including in a circle

feedback: Hinge joints, such as the elbow and knee, mainly allow flexion and extension

questions.text: What connects a muscle to a bone? Give the term.
questions.solution: Tendons attach muscles to bones; ligaments join bone to bone
questions.hint: The Achilles is a famous example at the back of the ankle

questions.text: What connects bone to bone at a joint? Give the term.
questions.solution: Ligaments are tough bands that join bone to bone and keep joints stable
questions.hint: Footballers can damage one called the ACL in the knee

questions.text: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.solution: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure
questions.hint: The first letter of these vessels matches the first letter of 'away'

feedback: Veins carry blood back towards the heart

questions.text: Give the name of the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange takes place.
questions.solution: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged across the thin walls of the alveoli (air sacs)
questions.hint: They are at the very end of the bronchioles

feedback.bronchioles: Bronchioles are the small tubes that lead to the air sacs

questions.text: Which of these is a function of the skeleton?
questions.solution: The skeleton gives support, protection, movement, blood cell production and mineral storage
questions.hint: Think about what the skull does for the brain

feedback: That is the job of the heart

questions.text: Which statement about flexion and extension is accurate?
questions.solution: Bending a joint (flexion) decreases the angle; straightening it (extension) increases the angle
questions.hint: Think about bending your elbow: does the angle get bigger or smaller?

options: Flexion decreases the angle at a joint; extension increases it
Flexion increases the angle at a joint; extension decreases it
Flexion moves a limb away from the midline; extension moves it towards the midline
Flexion is turning around; extension is moving in a circle
feedback: That describes abduction and adduction

questions.text: Which movement takes a limb away from the midline of the body? Give the term.
questions.solution: Abduction moves a limb away from the midline, as in the outward phase of a star jump
questions.hint: When someone is taken away, they are 'abducted'

feedback.adduction: Adduction moves a limb towards the midline

questions.text: At the elbow, which muscle is the agonist when the arm bends during a bicep curl?
questions.solution: During elbow flexion the biceps contract as the agonist and the triceps relax as the antagonist
questions.hint: The muscle that shortens to bend the elbow is at the front of the upper arm

feedback: The triceps is the antagonist during flexion; it is the agonist when the elbow extends

questions.text: Which statement about veins is accurate?
questions.solution: Veins return blood to the heart at low pressure and contain valves to prevent backflow
questions.hint: Blood in veins is at low pressure, so something must stop it flowing backwards

options: Veins carry blood away from the heart at high pressure
Veins are one cell thick for gas exchange
Veins carry blood towards the heart and have valves to stop backflow
Veins have the thickest, most muscular walls
feedback: That describes arteries
That describes capillaries

questions.text: Give the type of respiration that takes place without oxygen and produces lactic acid.
questions.solution: Anaerobic respiration releases energy without oxygen and produces lactic acid
questions.hint: 'An' at the start of a word means 'without'

feedback.aerobic: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and produces no lactic acid

questions.text: Which type of bone are the vertebrae?
questions.solution: Vertebrae are irregular bones: their complex shape protects the spinal cord
questions.hint: Their shape does not fit the other groups

feedback: Long bones include the femur and humerus
Flat bones include the cranium, ribs and sternum

questions.text: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygenated blood to the body through the aorta?
questions.solution: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood out through the aorta to the body
questions.hint: Ventricles pump blood out of the heart; which side carries oxygenated blood?

feedback: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs
The left atrium receives blood from the lungs

questions.text: A footballer kicks a ball. As the leg straightens at the knee, which movement happens?
questions.solution: Straightening the knee to kick increases the angle at the joint: extension
questions.hint: Is the angle at the knee getting bigger or smaller?

feedback: Flexion is bending the knee, as in the back-swing before the kick

questions.text: A sprinter pushes off onto their toes from the blocks. Which movement happens at the ankle?
questions.solution: Pointing the toes or pushing onto the toes is plantar flexion
questions.hint: Is the foot pointing down or pulling up towards the shin?

feedback: Dorsiflexion pulls the toes up towards the shin

questions.text: Which type of joint lets the head turn from side to side, between the atlas and axis vertebrae?
questions.solution: The joint between the atlas and axis in the neck is a pivot joint, allowing rotation
questions.hint: This joint allows rotation, like shaking your head to say 'no'

questions.text: A cricket bowler swings their arm in a full circle at the shoulder. Give the term for this movement.
questions.solution: Moving a limb so that it draws a circle is circumduction
questions.hint: It begins with 'circum', meaning around

feedback.rotation: Rotation is turning a limb around its own long axis; drawing a circle is circumduction

questions.text: During exercise, what happens to heart rate and stroke volume?
questions.solution: Heart rate and stroke volume both rise during exercise, so cardiac output (HR × SV) increases
questions.hint: Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume

options: Both increase, so cardiac output increases
Both decrease, so cardiac output decreases
Heart rate increases, but cardiac output falls

questions.text: Name the dome-shaped muscle under the lungs that contracts and flattens when you breathe in.
questions.solution: The diaphragm contracts and flattens when you inhale, making the chest cavity bigger
questions.hint: It separates the chest from the abdomen

questions.text: An 800 m runner sprints flat out for the last 200 m. Their legs start to feel heavy and they slow down. Which substance has built up in their muscles?
questions.solution: Working anaerobically at high intensity produces lactic acid, which causes muscle fatigue
questions.hint: This substance is produced when muscles work without enough oxygen

questions.text: A performer's heart rate is 150 bpm and their stroke volume is 100 ml. What is their cardiac output? Give the answer in litres per minute (1 litre = 1000 ml).
questions.solution: Cardiac output = HR × SV = 150 × 100 = 15 000 ml/min = 15 litres per minute
questions.hint: Multiply heart rate by stroke volume, then convert ml to litres

mistakes.feedback: That is in ml per minute; divide by 1000 to get litres

questions.text: A student's tidal volume is 0.5 litres and they take 12 breaths per minute. Minute ventilation = tidal volume × breathing rate. What is their minute ventilation in litres per minute?
questions.solution: Minute ventilation = 0.5 × 12 = 6 litres per minute
questions.hint: Multiply the volume of one breath by the number of breaths per minute

questions.text: Which list shows the path of air into the lungs in the correct order?
questions.solution: Air passes through the mouth or nose, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles and finally the alveoli
questions.hint: The tubes get narrower and narrower until they reach the air sacs

options: Mouth or nose, bronchi, trachea, alveoli, bronchioles
Trachea, mouth or nose, bronchioles, bronchi, alveoli
Mouth or nose, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli
Mouth or nose, trachea, alveoli, bronchioles, bronchi

questions.text: Why do arteries have thick, elastic, muscular walls?
questions.solution: Arteries carry blood at high pressure straight from the heart, so they need thick, elastic walls
questions.hint: Think about the pressure of blood leaving the heart

options: To let gases diffuse through them
To slow blood down so it can return to the heart
To store oxygen for later use
To cope with the high pressure of blood pumped from the heart
feedback: Gas exchange happens through thin-walled capillaries

questions.text: Which short-term effect of exercise on the respiratory system is accurate?
questions.solution: During exercise we breathe faster and more deeply to take in more oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
questions.hint: The muscles need more oxygen during exercise

options: Breathing rate and depth of breathing (tidal volume) both increase
Tidal volume decreases to save energy
Breathing rate falls during a sprint

questions.text: Give the term (or its abbreviation) for the extra oxygen used after exercise to recover, for example to remove lactic acid.
questions.solution: EPOC (excess post-exercise oxygen consumption), sometimes called oxygen debt, is used to recover after exercise
questions.hint: It is the reason you keep breathing hard after a sprint finishes

questions.text: Which muscle fibre type is best suited to a marathon runner?
questions.solution: Slow twitch (type I) fibres contract slowly, use oxygen well and resist fatigue, so they suit endurance events
questions.hint: Marathons need fibres that resist fatigue for a long time

feedback: Type IIx fibres are powerful but tire very quickly, suiting sprints

questions.text: Why does a long-distance runner develop more capillaries around their muscles after months of training?
questions.solution: More capillaries mean more oxygen can reach the muscles and more waste can be removed, improving endurance
questions.hint: Capillaries are where gases are exchanged with the muscles

options: Capillarisation makes the heart beat faster at rest
Capillarisation reduces the amount of blood in the body
Capillarisation increases oxygen delivery to the muscles and the removal of carbon dioxide
Capillarisation stops lactic acid forming at any intensity

questions.text: Why is the wall of the left ventricle thicker than the wall of the right ventricle?
questions.solution: The left ventricle must pump blood around the whole body, so it has a thicker muscular wall
questions.hint: Compare where each ventricle sends its blood

options: The left ventricle pumps blood only to the lungs
The left ventricle receives blood from the body
The left ventricle contains more valves
The left ventricle pumps blood all around the body, which needs more force than pumping to the lungs
feedback: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs

questions.text: During a 400 m race at maximum effort, which type of respiration mainly supplies energy, and what is a by-product?
questions.solution: High-intensity work like a flat-out 400 m relies mainly on anaerobic respiration, which produces lactic acid
questions.hint: At maximum intensity, the muscles cannot get enough oxygen

feedback: Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water, not lactic acid

questions.text: Which long-term effect of regular aerobic training is accurate?
questions.solution: Training enlarges and strengthens the heart, so stroke volume rises and resting heart rate falls (bradycardia)
questions.hint: A stronger heart pumps more blood with each beat

options: A higher resting heart rate, as the heart becomes weaker
A lower resting heart rate, as stroke volume increases
A smaller heart and lower stroke volume

questions.text: As a weight is lowered slowly in a bicep curl, which type of contraction happens in the biceps?
questions.solution: The biceps lengthen under tension to control the weight on the way down: an eccentric contraction
questions.hint: The muscle is getting longer but is still working to control the weight

feedback: Concentric contraction is when the muscle shortens, as when lifting the weight
The biceps must still work, or the weight would drop

questions.text: Which type of muscle contraction keeps the muscle the same length, for example when holding a plank? Give the term.
questions.solution: In an isometric (static) contraction the muscle is under tension but does not change length
questions.hint: 'Iso' means same and 'metric' means length

feedback.isotonic: Isotonic contractions change the muscle's length

questions.text: Which statement about gas exchange at the alveoli is accurate?
questions.solution: Gases diffuse from high to low concentration: oxygen into the blood, carbon dioxide out into the alveoli
questions.hint: Gases move from a high concentration to a low concentration

options: Carbon dioxide diffuses from the alveoli into the blood; oxygen diffuses from the blood into the alveoli
Both gases are pumped by the heart into the alveoli
Gases only pass through the trachea wall
Oxygen diffuses from the alveoli into the blood; carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into the alveoli
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which fitness test measures flexibility?
questions.solution: The sit and reach test measures flexibility of the lower back and hamstrings
questions.hint: The test involves reaching forwards along a box

feedback: The handgrip dynamometer measures strength

questions.text: Which fitness test measures cardiovascular (aerobic) endurance?
questions.solution: The multi-stage fitness (bleep) test measures cardiovascular endurance
questions.hint: This test gets harder as the bleeps get faster

feedback: The ruler drop test measures reaction time
The stork stand measures balance

questions.text: In the FITT principle, what does the F stand for? Give the word.
questions.solution: FITT stands for frequency, intensity, time and type
questions.hint: It is about how often you train

questions.text: Which component of fitness is the ability to change direction quickly while staying in control? Give the component.
questions.solution: Agility is the ability to change body position or direction quickly with control
questions.hint: It is tested by the Illinois run

feedback.balance: Balance is keeping the body's centre of mass over the base of support

questions.text: Which type of training uses a series of different exercises at different stations? Give the type.
questions.solution: Circuit training uses a series of exercise stations
questions.hint: You move round the stations in a loop

questions.text: What is the first phase of a warm-up?
questions.solution: A warm-up starts with a pulse raiser (gentle jogging), then stretching, then skill-based practice
questions.hint: The first phase gradually increases heart rate

questions.text: Which type of training, whose name means 'speed play', involves changes of pace and terrain? Give the Swedish term.
questions.solution: Fartlek ('speed play') mixes changes of speed and terrain in continuous running
questions.hint: It is a Swedish word

questions.text: Which statement about strength and power is accurate?
questions.solution: Strength is the force a muscle can apply; power = strength × speed
questions.hint: Which one involves doing something quickly as well as forcefully?

options: Power is the maximum force a muscle can apply; strength is power combined with speed
Power is the ability to keep going for a long time
Strength and power mean exactly the same thing
Strength is the maximum force a muscle can apply; power is strength combined with speed
feedback: That is endurance

questions.text: Which fitness test measures reaction time?
questions.solution: In the ruler drop test, you catch a falling ruler as quickly as possible, measuring reaction time
questions.hint: Someone drops an object and you must catch it

feedback: The Harvard step test measures cardiovascular fitness
The vertical jump measures power

questions.text: Which principle of training says that fitness is lost when training stops? Give the term.
questions.solution: Reversibility means fitness gains are lost if training stops
questions.hint: The gains are 'reversed'

questions.text: What does progressive overload mean?
questions.solution: Progressive overload gradually increases the demands on the body so fitness keeps improving
questions.hint: The key word is 'gradually'

options: Training as hard as possible every day
Gradually increasing the training load so the body keeps adapting
Training in the same way every session
feedback: That risks overtraining and injury

questions.text: Which fitness test measures power?
questions.solution: The vertical jump test measures (leg) power
questions.hint: Power is strength combined with speed: which test is explosive?

feedback: The Cooper run measures cardiovascular endurance

questions.text: Which component of fitness is measured by the stork stand test? Give the component.
questions.solution: The stork stand test measures (static) balance
questions.hint: You stand on one leg for as long as possible

questions.text: Which type of training uses bounding, hopping and depth jumps to develop power?
questions.solution: Plyometrics uses explosive jumps and bounds to develop power
questions.hint: This training involves a quick stretch of the muscle followed by an explosive movement

questions.text: Using maximum heart rate = 220 − age, what is the maximum heart rate of a 16-year-old? Give the answer in bpm.
questions.hint: Subtract the age from 220

mistakes.feedback: Subtract the age from 220; do not add it

questions.text: A 20-year-old's maximum heart rate is 200 bpm. The aerobic training zone is 60–80% of maximum heart rate. What is the lower limit of the zone in bpm?
questions.hint: Find 60% of 200

mistakes.feedback: 160 bpm is 80%, the upper limit of the aerobic zone

questions.text: A rower trains at a steady, moderate pace for 40 minutes without any rest. Which type of training is this?
questions.solution: Steady exercise for a long time without rest is continuous training, which develops aerobic endurance
questions.hint: The pace does not change and there are no rest periods

feedback: Fartlek involves changes of pace

questions.text: A sprinter runs 6 × 50 m flat out with 2 minutes of rest between each run. Which type of training is this?
questions.solution: Periods of hard work separated by rest periods is interval training
questions.hint: Work periods are separated by planned rest

questions.text: A rugby player wants to improve strength. Which type of weight training is most suitable?
questions.solution: High loads with low repetitions develop strength; light loads with many repetitions develop muscular endurance
questions.hint: Strength is about maximum force

feedback: Light weights with many repetitions develop muscular endurance

questions.text: Which principle of training means matching training to the demands of the sport or activity? Give the term.
questions.solution: Specificity means training should match the demands of the activity
questions.hint: A swimmer should train mainly by swimming

questions.text: In which plane of movement does a forward roll take place?
questions.solution: Forward rolls, somersaults and running happen in the sagittal plane, which divides the body into left and right
questions.hint: This plane divides the body into left and right sides

feedback: The frontal plane is for sideways movements such as a cartwheel
The transverse plane is for turning movements such as a full twist

questions.text: An 18-year-old's maximum heart rate is 202 bpm. What is 80% of their maximum heart rate, the top of the aerobic training zone? Give the answer to the nearest whole number in bpm.
questions.solution: 80% of 202 = 0.8 × 202 = 161.6, which rounds to 162 bpm
questions.hint: Multiply 202 by 0.8, then round

mistakes.feedback: 121 bpm is about 60%, the lower limit of the aerobic zone

questions.text: A student trains at 85% of their maximum heart rate. Which training zone is this?
questions.solution: 85% is between 80% and 90%, so it is in the anaerobic training zone
questions.hint: Compare 85% with the limits of each zone

questions.text: A footballer's plan changes from 2 to 3 training sessions a week. Which part of FITT has changed?
questions.solution: The number of sessions per week is frequency
questions.hint: This part of FITT is about how often

feedback: Intensity is how hard you work
Time is how long each session lasts

questions.text: A swimmer cannot train for six weeks because of an injury, and their fitness falls. Which principle explains this?
questions.solution: When training stops, fitness gains are lost: reversibility
questions.hint: The gains go into reverse

questions.text: In which plane of movement does a cartwheel mainly take place?
questions.solution: Sideways movements such as cartwheels and star jumps happen in the frontal plane, which divides the body front and back
questions.hint: The movement is sideways

feedback: The sagittal plane is for forward and backward movements such as a forward roll

questions.text: A hockey player scores poorly on the sit and reach test (8 cm) but well on the multi-stage fitness test (level 11). Which training should they add?
questions.solution: The weak area is flexibility (sit and reach), so stretching would target it
questions.hint: Find the weaker test result and the component it measures

questions.text: During a bicep curl, the effort from the biceps is between the fulcrum (elbow) and the load (hand). Which class of lever is this? Give the class (first, second or third).
questions.solution: Effort in the middle makes a third-class lever, the most common lever in the body
questions.hint: Remember 1-2-3, F-L-E: what is in the middle for each class?

feedback.second: In a second-class lever the load is in the middle

questions.text: Why should a long-distance runner not rely only on heavy weight training with few repetitions?
questions.solution: Training must match the activity (specificity); distance runners need aerobic and muscular endurance
questions.hint: Which principle is about matching training to the activity?

options: Heavy weights build aerobic endurance too quickly
Heavy, low-repetition work does not match the demands of their event, so it breaks the principle of specificity

questions.text: Which statement about plyometrics is accurate?
questions.solution: Plyometrics stretches the muscle (eccentric) then contracts it explosively (concentric), developing power
questions.hint: Think about landing from a box and immediately jumping up

options: Plyometrics is steady, low-intensity work for 30 minutes
An eccentric contraction is followed quickly by a concentric contraction to develop power

questions.text: Going up onto your toes (plantar flexion at the ankle) uses which class of lever, and what is its advantage?
questions.solution: With the ball of the foot as the fulcrum, the load (body weight) is in the middle: a second-class lever, which has a mechanical advantage
questions.hint: The fulcrum is the ball of the foot and the effort comes from the calf muscle

options: First class, with a large range of movement
Third class, with a mechanical advantage
Second class, with a large range of movement but no mechanical advantage
Second class, with a mechanical advantage so a large load can be moved with little effort

questions.text: Why is a cool down useful after intense exercise?
questions.solution: Light exercise and stretching after activity help remove lactic acid and bring heart rate down gradually
questions.hint: Think about what happens to heart rate and lactic acid after exercise

options: A cool down helps remove lactic acid and gradually returns the heart rate to resting levels
A cool down increases lactic acid
A cool down raises body temperature before exercise
A cool down makes the next session unnecessary

questions.text: Why might an endurance athlete train at high altitude?
questions.solution: At altitude there is less oxygen available, so the body adapts by making more red blood cells
questions.hint: Is there more or less oxygen available high up?

options: There is more oxygen at high altitude
Lower oxygen levels make the body produce more red blood cells, improving oxygen-carrying capacity
Altitude training reduces the number of red blood cells
feedback: There is less oxygen available at high altitude

questions.text: Which component of fitness combines strength and speed? Give the component.
questions.solution: Power = strength × speed, as in a long jump take-off
questions.hint: It is tested by the vertical jump

questions.text: A gymnast's sessions are varied with new exercises and venues to prevent boredom. Which principle does this apply?
questions.solution: Avoiding tedium means varying training so the performer stays motivated
questions.hint: The principle is named after boredom itself

questions.text: What is an open skill?
questions.solution: Open skills are affected by the environment (opponents, teammates, conditions), so the performer must adapt
questions.hint: Think about a pass when defenders are moving around you

options: A skill affected by a changing environment, such as passing in football
A skill not affected by the environment, such as a basketball free throw
A skill that uses only small muscles
feedback: That is a closed skill

questions.text: Which of these is an example of a closed skill?
questions.solution: A vault is performed in a stable, predictable environment, so it is closed
questions.hint: Look for the skill that is not affected by opponents or teammates

options: Dribbling past a defender in hockey

questions.text: Which type of guidance involves the coach physically moving the performer's body through the movement? Give the type.
questions.solution: Manual guidance is when the coach physically guides the performer
questions.hint: The coach uses their hands

feedback.mechanical: Mechanical guidance uses equipment such as floats or harnesses

questions.text: In SMART targets, what does the M stand for? Give the word.
questions.solution: M stands for measurable: progress towards the target can be measured
questions.hint: You need to be able to check whether the target has been reached

questions.text: What is a gross skill?
questions.solution: Gross skills use large muscle groups and are powerful; fine skills use small muscles and precision
questions.hint: Think of big, powerful movements

options: A skill that uses small muscle groups for precision, such as a dart throw
A skill that needs no decisions
A skill that uses large muscle groups, such as the shot put
feedback: That is a fine skill

questions.text: Which type of motivation comes from within the performer, such as enjoyment and pride? Give the type.
questions.solution: Intrinsic motivation comes from inside, such as enjoyment or satisfaction
questions.hint: 'In' means inside

feedback.extrinsic: Extrinsic motivation comes from outside, such as trophies or praise

questions.text: Which type of guidance uses demonstrations, videos or diagrams?
questions.solution: Visual guidance shows the performer what to do, through demonstrations, videos or diagrams
questions.hint: You use your eyes to take it in

feedback: Verbal guidance uses spoken instructions

questions.text: Which statement about intrinsic and extrinsic feedback is accurate?
questions.solution: Intrinsic feedback is what the performer feels; extrinsic feedback comes from others, such as a coach or video
questions.hint: 'Intrinsic' means coming from within

options: Intrinsic feedback comes from the performer's own senses; extrinsic feedback comes from outside, such as a coach
Extrinsic feedback comes from the performer's own senses; intrinsic feedback comes from a coach
Both come only from a scoreboard
Both are only given before a performance
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which statement about a skill and an ability is accurate?
questions.solution: Skills are learned through practice; abilities are inherited traits that help us learn skills
questions.hint: Which one can you be born with?

options: An ability is learned; a skill is inherited
A skill is learned; an ability is inherited
Skills are only physical; abilities are only mental
Skills and abilities mean exactly the same thing
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which type of guidance uses equipment such as a float or a harness to support the performer? Give the type.
questions.solution: Mechanical guidance uses equipment to support the performer
questions.hint: Equipment is used instead of the coach's hands

feedback.manual: Manual guidance is when the coach physically moves the performer

questions.text: Which of these is an example of extrinsic motivation?
questions.solution: Extrinsic motivation comes from outside rewards such as trophies, money or praise
questions.hint: Look for a reward given by someone else

options: Playing for a sense of achievement
Playing for the love of the sport

questions.text: Which type of feedback is given during the performance?
questions.solution: Concurrent feedback is given during the performance; terminal feedback is given afterwards
questions.hint: 'Concurrent' means happening at the same time

feedback: Terminal feedback is given after the performance

questions.text: In SMART targets, what does the S stand for? Give the word.
questions.solution: S stands for specific: the target is clear and focused on one thing
questions.hint: The target must be clear and focused

questions.text: Which of these skills is self-paced?
questions.solution: The server decides when to start, so a serve is self-paced; the others depend on an opponent or teammate
questions.hint: Who decides when the skill starts?

options: Hitting a bowled ball in cricket

questions.text: A coach tells a beginner: 'Keep your elbow high when you swim front crawl.' Which type of guidance is this?
questions.solution: Spoken instructions are verbal guidance
questions.hint: The coach is speaking to the swimmer

questions.text: A golfer feels that a putt was hit too hard as soon as they strike the ball. Which type of feedback is this?
questions.solution: Feeling the movement through your own senses is intrinsic feedback
questions.hint: Nobody else has told the golfer anything

questions.text: A rugby player is too anxious before a match. Which technique could lower their arousal?
questions.solution: Deep breathing, mental rehearsal and positive self-talk are stress management techniques that lower arousal
questions.hint: Which option would make the player calmer?

questions.text: A swimmer's coach says: 'Your time was 1 minute 5 seconds.' Give the type of feedback that tells a performer the outcome (knowledge of …).
questions.solution: Feedback about the outcome, such as a time or score, is knowledge of results
questions.hint: It is about the outcome, not the technique

feedback.knowledge of performance: Knowledge of performance is about technique, not the outcome

questions.text: An archer needs a steady hand and calm focus. According to the inverted-U theory, which arousal level suits archery best?
questions.solution: Fine, precise skills such as archery are best performed at a low level of arousal
questions.hint: Fine skills need a calm performer

questions.text: A target says: 'I will run 5 km in under 25 minutes by the end of June.' Which part of SMART is shown by 'by the end of June'?
questions.solution: A deadline makes the target time-bound
questions.hint: Which part of SMART sets a deadline?

questions.text: Which skill classification describes a skill that uses small muscle groups for precise movements, such as a snooker shot? Give the term.
questions.solution: Fine skills use small muscle groups and need precision
questions.hint: It is the opposite of gross

feedback.gross: Gross skills use large muscle groups

questions.text: A beginner gymnast is learning a handspring. Which combination of guidance is most suitable at first?
questions.solution: Beginners learn well from demonstrations, and manual support keeps them safe in a risky skill
questions.hint: Beginners need to see the skill and be kept safe

options: Only verbal guidance with lots of technical detail
No guidance, so they discover it themselves
A visual demonstration with manual support from the coach
Video analysis of their own elite performances
feedback: Too much detail can overload a beginner

questions.text: Which statement about the inverted-U theory is accurate?
questions.solution: The inverted-U theory says there is an optimum (moderate) level of arousal; too little or too much harms performance
questions.hint: Picture the shape of an upside-down U on a graph

options: Performance always improves as arousal rises
Performance is best when arousal is lowest
Arousal has no effect on performance
Performance improves as arousal rises up to an optimum point, then gets worse

questions.text: Where is a penalty kick in football on the open–closed continuum?
questions.solution: A penalty is mostly closed: the ball is still and the taker chooses when to start, though the goalkeeper adds some unpredictability
questions.hint: Is the ball moving, and who decides when to start?

options: Towards closed, as the environment is mostly stable and the taker starts when ready
Completely open, as the environment changes constantly
Completely open, as teammates are moving
Exactly in the middle, as it has no environment

questions.text: Which of these is an example of knowledge of performance?
questions.solution: Knowledge of performance is feedback about technique, not the outcome
questions.hint: Look for feedback about how the skill was performed

options: The scoreboard shows the throw went 30 m
A coach explains that the arm action in a throw was too low

questions.text: Which stress management technique involves picturing yourself performing a skill successfully in your mind? Give the term.
questions.solution: Mental rehearsal (visualisation or imagery) means picturing a successful performance in your mind
questions.hint: You 'see' the performance in your head

questions.text: Which list shows the stages of the information processing model in the correct order?
questions.solution: Information comes in (input), a decision is made, the movement is performed (output) and feedback follows
questions.hint: What must happen before a decision can be made?

questions.text: A footballer receives constant shouted instructions from the touchline while playing. Which type of feedback is this?
questions.solution: It is given during play (concurrent) by someone else (extrinsic)
questions.hint: Decide when it is given and who it comes from

questions.text: A beginner receives only negative feedback. What is the most likely effect?
questions.solution: Beginners need encouragement; too much negative feedback can lower motivation and confidence
questions.hint: Think about how constant criticism affects confidence

options: Their motivation may drop, so beginners usually need mainly positive feedback
Feedback has no effect on beginners

questions.text: Why can experienced performers make better use of intrinsic feedback than beginners?
questions.solution: Experienced performers have a clear feel for the correct technique, so their own senses tell them about errors
questions.hint: Think about what a performer needs to know to judge their own movement

options: Beginners can always tell when a movement is wrong
Experts know what a correct movement feels like, so they can detect their own errors
Intrinsic feedback comes from the coach
feedback: Feedback from a coach is extrinsic

questions.text: A boxer becomes over-aroused just before a bout. According to the inverted-U theory, what is likely?
questions.solution: Past the optimum, extra arousal causes performance to fall, even in sports that need high arousal
questions.hint: Where is 'over-aroused' on the inverted-U curve?

options: Performance will be at its best, as arousal is as high as possible
Performance may get worse, as arousal has gone past the optimum point
Performance will keep improving without limit

questions.text: Which of these targets is SMART?
questions.solution: A SMART target is specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time-bound
questions.hint: Look for a target with a measurement and a deadline

options: Run faster than everyone in the world this year
Improve my 100 m time from 14.0 s to 13.5 s within 8 weeks

questions.text: Why might a coach use mental rehearsal with a nervous high jumper?
questions.solution: Mental rehearsal lowers anxiety, builds confidence and helps focus on the key parts of the skill
questions.hint: Think about what mental rehearsal does to nerves

options: Picturing a successful jump can lower anxiety and improve focus
Mental rehearsal raises arousal to the highest level
Mental rehearsal replaces physical training completely

questions.text: Which type of feedback is given after the performance has finished? Give the term.
questions.solution: Terminal feedback is given after the performance has finished
questions.hint: It comes at the end, like the last stop of a bus route

feedback.concurrent: Concurrent feedback is given during the performance

questions.text: Which statement about a complex skill is accurate?
questions.solution: Complex skills need many decisions and high concentration; basic skills need few decisions
questions.hint: Think about how many decisions the performer has to make

options: A complex skill needs few decisions and is simple to learn
A complex skill needs many decisions and a lot of attention, such as passing under pressure in rugby
A complex skill is always a closed skill
A complex skill uses only small muscle groups

questions.text: What is the commercialisation of sport?
questions.solution: Commercialisation means sport being managed and promoted for profit, through sponsorship, media and merchandise
questions.hint: The word comes from 'commerce', meaning business

options: Managing and promoting sport to make a profit

questions.text: What is sportsmanship?
questions.solution: Sportsmanship means fair play and respect, such as shaking hands with opponents
questions.hint: Think about shaking hands after a match

options: Bending the rules to gain an advantage
Playing fairly and showing respect to opponents and officials
feedback: That is gamesmanship

questions.text: What term means bending the rules to gain an advantage without actually breaking them, such as wasting time? Give the term.
questions.solution: Gamesmanship is bending the rules, such as time-wasting, without breaking them
questions.hint: It sounds like sportsmanship but begins with a different word

feedback.sportsmanship: Sportsmanship is fair play, the opposite of this

questions.text: What is a sponsor in sport?
questions.solution: Sponsors give money, equipment or services in exchange for advertising and publicity
questions.hint: Think about logos on football shirts

options: An official who enforces the rules
A coach who trains the team
A company or person that provides money, kit or services in return for publicity
A fan who buys a ticket

questions.text: Which groups make up the 'golden triangle' in sport?
questions.solution: The golden triangle is the link between sport, sponsorship and the media
questions.hint: Think about money, publicity and the sport itself

questions.text: Give the abbreviation for the organisation that leads the worldwide fight against drugs in sport.
questions.solution: WADA is the World Anti-Doping Agency
questions.hint: It is a four-letter abbreviation; the first word is 'World'

questions.text: Which of these is a physical health benefit of regular exercise?
questions.solution: Regular exercise strengthens the heart and lowers the risk of heart disease
questions.hint: Which option is a benefit, not a problem?

options: A lower risk of heart disease

questions.text: Which type of performance-enhancing drug increases muscle size and strength?
questions.solution: Anabolic steroids increase muscle mass and strength and speed up recovery, but have serious side effects
questions.hint: These drugs are copies of the hormone testosterone

feedback: Beta blockers calm nerves and steady the hands
Narcotic analgesics mask pain

questions.text: Which performance-enhancing drug is used to calm nerves and steady the hands, for example in archery or shooting?
questions.solution: Beta blockers lower heart rate and reduce shaking, helping in precision sports
questions.hint: These drugs slow the heart rate down

feedback: Stimulants increase alertness and heart rate

questions.text: EPO is a hormone that increases red blood cell production. Give its full name.
questions.solution: EPO is erythropoietin, which increases red blood cells and oxygen-carrying capacity
questions.hint: It begins with 'erythro', meaning red

questions.text: Which of these is a mental (emotional) health benefit of exercise?
questions.solution: Exercise releases chemicals such as serotonin and endorphins, which reduce stress and improve mood
questions.hint: Mental benefits are about how you feel

options: Reduced stress and a better mood
feedback: Stronger bones is a physical benefit

questions.text: Which of these is a social health benefit of exercise?
questions.solution: Social benefits include making friends, teamwork and a sense of belonging
questions.hint: Social benefits involve other people

options: Making friends and working with others
feedback: Lower stress is a mental (emotional) benefit

questions.text: Which type of drug increases alertness and reduces tiredness and is banned in competition? Give the drug type.
questions.solution: Stimulants increase alertness and reduce tiredness; they are banned in competition
questions.hint: These drugs 'stimulate' the nervous system

questions.text: Which of these is a disadvantage of media coverage for a sport?
questions.solution: TV companies may change event times, which can be inconvenient for players and fans
questions.hint: Look for the option that causes a problem

options: More people learn about the sport
Kick-off times may be changed to suit TV schedules

questions.text: A cyclist has some of their own blood removed, stored, and then put back before a race. What is this called?
questions.solution: Re-injecting stored blood increases red blood cells and oxygen-carrying capacity: blood doping, which is banned
questions.hint: It increases the number of red blood cells illegally

questions.text: A tennis player takes a long time between points to upset their opponent's rhythm. What is this an example of?
questions.solution: Deliberately wasting time to unsettle an opponent bends the rules: gamesmanship
questions.hint: The player is not breaking a rule, but is not being fair either

questions.text: A team kicks the ball out of play so that an injured opponent can get treatment. Give the term for this kind of behaviour.
questions.solution: Stopping play for an injured opponent shows fair play and respect: sportsmanship
questions.hint: The team gives up an advantage for the sake of an opponent

feedback.gamesmanship: Gamesmanship is bending the rules to gain an advantage

questions.text: A tennis player trains in hot weather without drinking. They feel dizzy and tired and have a headache. What is the most likely cause?
questions.solution: Losing water through sweat without replacing it leads to dehydration, causing dizziness, headaches and fatigue
questions.hint: Think about what was lost through sweating

questions.text: Endurance athletes eat extra carbohydrate in the days before a long race to fill their glycogen stores. Give the name of this practice.
questions.solution: Carbohydrate loading increases glycogen stores in muscles before endurance events
questions.hint: Think of 'loading up' with a type of nutrient

questions.text: Which of these is an effect of dehydration on performance?
questions.solution: Dehydration thickens the blood, raises heart rate, slows reactions and makes overheating more likely
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the blood when the body loses water

options: A higher heart rate and slower reactions
Thinner blood that flows more easily
feedback: Dehydration makes the blood thicker, not thinner

questions.text: A company pays to have its logo on a team's shirts. What is this an example of? Give the term.
questions.solution: This is sponsorship: money in return for publicity
questions.hint: Think about logos on football shirts and what the company gets in return

questions.text: A gym costs £40 a month and the nearest swimming pool is 20 miles away. Which factors are most likely to reduce a teenager's participation?
questions.solution: The information given is about price and distance, so cost and access are the barriers
questions.hint: Look at what the information in the question tells you

questions.text: Which statement about the effect of sponsorship on a sport is accurate?
questions.solution: Sponsorship brings in money, but sponsors may want a say, for example in kit or event timing
questions.hint: Think about both an advantage and a disadvantage

options: Sponsorship always reduces the money available to the sport
Sponsorship has no effect on performers
Only amateur sports can be sponsored
Sponsorship can fund facilities and events, but the sponsor may try to influence decisions

questions.text: An athlete tests positive for a banned substance. Which consequence is likely?
questions.solution: Doping leads to bans, stripped medals, lost sponsorship and a damaged reputation
questions.hint: Think about the punishments for cheating

options: A ban from competition and the loss of medals or titles
Automatic selection for the next event

questions.text: Why might a sponsor end its deal with an athlete who has been banned for doping?
questions.solution: Sponsors want positive publicity; being linked to a drug cheat could harm their image and sales
questions.hint: What does a sponsor want in return for its money?

options: The sponsor wants more coverage of doping
Negative publicity could damage the sponsor's reputation
The athlete has become too successful

questions.text: Why are diuretics banned in sport?
questions.solution: Diuretics increase urine production, which can dilute or hide other banned substances
questions.hint: They make the body produce more urine

options: Diuretics can be used to mask (hide) other banned drugs
Diuretics increase the red blood cell count
feedback: That describes anabolic steroids

questions.text: Which statement about the World Health Organization definition of health is accurate?
questions.solution: The WHO defines health as a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease
questions.hint: The definition has three parts

options: Health means only being free from illness
Health is the same as fitness
Health is complete physical, mental and social well-being, not just the absence of disease

questions.text: Give the term for a lifestyle with little or no physical activity.
questions.solution: A sedentary lifestyle involves little or no physical activity
questions.hint: It comes from the Latin word for 'sitting'

questions.text: Which statement about the 'golden triangle' is accurate?
questions.solution: The three parts depend on each other: each one helps the other two
questions.hint: Think about how each corner helps the other two

options: Media coverage attracts sponsors, sponsorship funds sport, and successful sport attracts more media
The media, sport and sponsors are completely independent
Sponsors pay the media to stop showing sport
Only amateur sport is part of the golden triangle

questions.text: Why might a talented performer from a low-income family take part less in some sports?
questions.solution: The cost of kit, fees and travel can be a barrier to participation
questions.hint: Think about the costs involved in taking part

options: Income has no effect on participation
Costs of equipment, travel and membership can be a barrier
Low-income families are not allowed to join clubs

questions.text: Which statement about beta blockers is accurate?
questions.solution: Beta blockers reduce heart rate and tremors, which could help in archery, shooting or snooker, so they are banned
questions.hint: Think about which sports need a very steady hand

options: Beta blockers raise heart rate to improve endurance
Beta blockers lower heart rate and reduce shaking, so they are banned in sports needing precision
Beta blockers are allowed in all sports

questions.text: Which statement about anabolic steroids is accurate?
questions.solution: Anabolic steroids increase muscle mass and recovery but have serious health risks and are banned
questions.hint: Consider both the effect and the health risks

options: Steroids calm nerves for precision sports
Steroids are allowed for performers under 18
Steroids increase muscle growth and speed up recovery, but can cause serious side effects such as heart and liver damage

questions.text: Why is hydration especially important when exercising in hot weather?
questions.solution: In heat we sweat more; without replacing fluid, blood becomes thicker and body temperature control suffers
questions.hint: Think about how the body cools itself down

options: More water is lost in sweat, so without drinking the blood thickens and the body overheats more easily
The body needs less water in hot weather
Sweating adds water to the blood

questions.text: How can the media have a positive effect on participation in sport?
questions.solution: Media coverage of successful role models can inspire people to try a sport
questions.hint: Think about the effect of watching a star perform well

options: Moving events to pay-TV makes them easier for everyone to watch
Showing role models can inspire people to take up a sport
Showing only a few sports makes all sports popular
Reporting only scandals encourages young people to join clubs

questions.text: Which term describes behaviour that goes against the rules and norms of sport, such as violence or doping? Give the term.
questions.solution: Deviance is behaviour that breaks the rules or norms of sport, such as violence or doping
questions.hint: It comes from 'deviate', meaning to move away from what is expected

feedback.gamesmanship: Gamesmanship bends the rules; doping and violence break them
